subject: OrchidPay SEV-2: rapid update and next-step commitments
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@orchidpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: OrchidPay production inference degradation (SEV-2) — initial notice

Alice —

Quick heads-up: we observed elevated 5xx errors and a ~700–900ms P95 increase on the production inference pool serving OrchidPay between 08:45–09:05 UTC. Impact appears limited to a subset of /v1/generate routes backed by the Llama-2-13B-q model. No data exfiltration suspected; requests and responses appear intact.

What we know now:
- Start time (observed): 2027-08-02T08:45:12Z
- Symptoms: transient 502/504 errors for ~7% of requests; P95 latency up from ~180ms to ~850ms
- Scope: calls routed to us-east-1 serving shard-7; customer impact reported by OrchidPay production by a single feature flag rollout

Immediate steps we've taken:
- Auto-roll back the recent Canary routing change to the previous routing profile (completed 09:05 PDT)
- Kicked off an incident bridge and ops triage (David leading)
- Enabled detailed logging and started collecting error traces/kv-cache metrics

Next steps / ask from you:
- Any business-critical windows today we should avoid planned restarts for?
- If you can share an example request id that hit the error, forward it and we’ll prioritize.

I'll keep you posted every 60 minutes or on material changes. David will follow with technical detail once we've triaged. Apologies for the disruption — we're treating this as SEV-2 with potential for escalation.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachment: initial-error-logs.txt (text stub)
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@orchidpay.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Urgent: OrchidPay production inference degradation (SEV-2) — initial notice

Alice / team — quick technical update from triage: we captured traces and logs for the affected window. Preliminary root-candidates:

1) KV-cache pressure: shard-7 shows a spike in KV cache evictions when the Canary routing increased concurrent long-context requests. Evictions correlate with elevated recompute time and higher GPU memory churn.
2) Background GC on the host kernel (driver-level) coincident with the same window for a subset of nodes — exacerbated by the model's attention pattern on this workload.

Mitigation actions completed:
- Rolled back the routing change (Ben did this at ~09:05 PDT).
- Throttled long-context requests for affected routes at the gateway for 30m to reduce pressure.
- Brought two spare inference workers online and rebalanced traffic away from shard-7.

Immediate impact: error rates back to baseline (~0.5%) and P95 latency trending down toward historic levels but still ~220–260ms while KV warming completes. We will continue monitoring over the next 3 hours.

Planned follow-ups:
- Collect and attach a focused set of error traces and op-level metrics (attachment: ops-triage-notes.txt).
- Run a controlled replay against a staging copy of the request pattern tonight to validate a long-term fix (we’ll schedule for 02:00 PDT).

If you have any request ids that failed during the window, please send them to me and I will correlate.

— David
David Kim
Senior Incident Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@orchidpay.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: OrchidPay CTO <cto@orchidpay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Urgent: OrchidPay production inference degradation (SEV-2) — initial notice

Ben / David —

Thanks for the rapid response. We observed user-facing errors (payment flow retries) for roughly 10 minutes and have customers who saw slowed page loads. We captured the following example request ids: rp_20270802_08_47_1111, rp_20270802_08_49_2222 — please correlate and share exact request/response outcomes so we can reconcile with our support tickets.

Two asks from OrchidPay leadership (cc'ing our CTO):
1) Please provide an executive note we can share internally and with our banking partners that summarizes impact, cause candidates, and next steps — our compliance team is asking for an initial incident note by EOD.
2) Clarify whether this incident triggers any SLA credit or remediation per our contract — we will expect an estimate of customer-facing exposure (number of requests & duration) and proposed commercial remedies.

We appreciate the swift rollback. How confident are you that the Canary routing change was the sole cause? If not sole cause, what additional mitigations will you implement to avoid recurrence?

— Alice
Alice Monroe
Head of Product, OrchidPay
alice.monroe@orchidpay.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@orchidpay.com>, Orchard Partner Team <cto@orchidpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: OrchidPay executive update: incident summary, customer impact, and commitments

Alice / OrchidPay leadership —

Thank you for raising this promptly and for the example request ids. Below is an executive summary we prepared for your internal distribution; please let me know if you want any language edited for partner/regulator communication.

Executive summary (for circulation) —
Impact window: 2027-08-02 08:45:12Z to 2027-08-02 09:12:34Z.
Customer impact: ~7–10% of targeted inference calls experienced 502/504 errors or elevated latency; OrchidPay reports user-visible retries in the payments checkout flow for ~10 minutes. No sensitive data was exposed.
Root-cause hypothesis: the Canary routing change increased concurrent long-context requests against shard-7, which triggered KV cache pressure and memory churn on a subset of hosts; this was amplified by coincident driver-level GC activity. Our rollback and traffic rebalancing restored baseline behavior.
Immediate remediation completed:
- Canary routing rollback at 09:05 PDT
- Throttling of long-context requests and rebalancing to spare workers
- Dedicated trace correlation for the example request ids (attached)

Committed next steps and timeline:
- Tonight 02:00 PDT: controlled replay in staging to reproduce and validate a durable mitigation (David leading) — outcome expected by 03:00 PDT and we will share results.
- Within 48 hours: deployment of targeted KV-cache tuning and kernel-level guardrails to reduce eviction storms.
- Within 5 business days: postmortem document with RCA, timeline, mitigations, and regression tests. We will share a draft for your review prior to publication.

Commercial / SLA: We recognize the customer impact and will follow the SLA review process. Our commercial team will calculate exposure (requests affected & duration) and propose remediation consistent with the contract by EOD Thursday.

Follow-up items for OrchidPay:
- Please reply if you want us to include a short customer-facing statement we can co-sign.
- Confirm a preferred time for a 30-minute follow-up sync after we complete the replay tomorrow evening.

Attachments: orchidpay-postmortem-plan.pdf (initial plan and timeline), ops-triage-notes.txt (technical traces and correlates).

We regret the disruption and appreciate the partnership — we will prioritize preventing recurrence.

Regards,

Marissa Cole
Strategic Accounts Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
